_comment: klt erc supply spec for layout/gain_cell_2t_array.gds -- the structural
power-delivery (T1 item 11, klayout-tools design-evidence-tiers.md)
evidence committed here per issue #39.
Run from the REPO ROOT (klt signoff re-reads the spec a report names
relative to its own cwd, so the report must record the root-relative path):
klt erc layout/gain_cell_2t_array.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--pdk sky130 --format json
-> committed as layout/gain_cell_2t_array.erc.result.json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry role: "gate" (klt erc's own contract,
docs/cli/erc.md 'Spec file'), so the accumulation starts at gate poly
66/20 (sky130A.lyp 'poly.drawing'; cross-checked against
klayout-tools' curated sky130 deck LAYER_NAMES (66, 20) ->
"poly.drawing"). active_layer: diff drawing 65/20 makes the per-gate
antenna denominator poly- intersect diff and not raw poly area (the
#1979 gate-area fix): the 4x4 array draws no tie-cell/decap/filler poly
at all, so today every poly net intersecting diff is a real gate, and
active_layer keeps that true by construction rather than by inspection.
- li1 67/20 ('li1.drawing') with label_layer 67/5: the GND text -- the
only supply label in the stream -- sits on li1.label 67/5 at the
guard-ring pin (-0.86, 3.08), and so do the 4 bl_<c>, 4 rbl_<c> and 16
sn_<r>_<c> texts (25 li1.label texts total). Declaring 67/5 is what
lets the erc.unconnected_net check read the GND label at all; the
signal texts ride along as cosmetic gates[].net names.
- met1 68/20 ('met1.drawing') with label_layer 68/5: the four wl_<r> and
four rwl_<r> routes strap on met1 and carry their 8 met1.label 68/5
texts there. Declaring met1 is required for the stack to cover every
routing level this block actually uses; 68/5 is its label companion.
- met2..met5 are deliberately absent from stackup: klt layers shows the
stream uses exactly 9 layer/datatype pairs (65/20 diff, 65/44 tap,
met1) -- no met2-or-above geometry exists, and a stackup entry naming
an absent layer would only add dead levels[0] rows.
- vias[]: licon1 66/44 bridges poly->li1 (every gate contact in this
design lands on li1), mcon 67/44 bridges li1->met1 (the word-line
straps). No via1..4: no met2+ geometry to bridge. The licon1 shapes
also landing on source/drain diffusion and on the tap ring are
harmless: diff (65/20) and tap (65/44) are not stackup roles, so those
via shapes simply connect the li1 stubs this model is built from.
- nets[]: GND is the ONLY declared net and the only supply. The 2T
bitcell (design/gain_cell_2t.spice, the LVS reference) is two nfet_01v8
whose third terminal is the bulk and whose .GLOBAL is GND: the array's
one rail is the substrate/bulk, tapped by the shared guard ring.
kind: "supply" is what makes a short against any other declared
supply report as the severe erc.supply_short (with one supply there is
no pair to short, so the zero count means exactly 'one island'), and
erc.unconnected_net fires on zero OR several islands -- zero findings
of either rule naming GND is exactly the one-electrical-island verdict
the T1 item grades. wl_<r>/rwl_<r>/bl_<c>/rbl_<c>/sn_<r>_<c> are signal
nets and are deliberately NOT declared: the item declares supplies,
and a signal declaration would only opt those nets into
erc.multiply_driven_net, which the item does not grade.
- ties[]: ONE substrate (p-substrate) tie, declared by well assertion
(klayout-tools#2255, docs/cli/erc.md 'A block with no drawn well at all').
sky130's psub is not a drawn GDS layer and this all-NMOS stream draws no
nwell (64/20 is absent), so there is no well polygon to name:
well_layer is null and well_boxes asserts the substrate region instead.
Because the assertion substitutes for a drawn layer, nothing in the
stream corroborates it, so it is derived from committed geometry and
kept as fine as the geometry allows:
- tap_layer 65/44 is sky130's tap-only layer (tap_is_dedicated: true), so
no tap_requires narrowing exists to be applied; connect_to: li1 is the
layer the tap's licon1 land on, i.e. the GND ring conductor.
- The only tap geometry in the stream is the shared guard ring: one
merged 65/44 polygon, outer edge (-1.07, -1.07)-(12.59, 7.23), inner
edge (-0.65, -0.65)-(12.17, 6.81) um (ring width 0.42 um; read from
gain_cell_2t_array.gds with klayout, not from the generator request).
well_boxes are its four edge strips (bottom, top, left, right), i.e.
the ring itself and not its enclosing rectangle. Adjacent strips merge
into one ring-shaped polygon, which must hold a tap reaching GND.
- What this does and does not claim: it asserts that the substrate under
the guard ring is tied to GND by a tap contact that reaches the GND
conductor. It does NOT claim that every point of the substrate inside
the ring is tied; that interior is tied to the ring through bulk
silicon, which klt erc does not model (docs/cli/erc.md, 'diffusion/
well continuity is not modeled'). Asserting the ring's enclosing box
would cover the whole top-cell extent and be skipped as
degenerate_well_assertion, so it is deliberately not used. The
independent device-aware cross-check for the interior is the array LVS
(gain_cell_2t_array.lvs.result.json: GND paired, bulk terminals matched).
- Falsifiability: if the strips are moved off the ring, or the tap
layer is removed from the stream, erc.missing_tie fires (negative
control recorded in the PR for issue #54).
